title: Neptune's Latitudinal Variations as Viewed with ALMA
question: How do Neptune's latitudinal brightness temperature variations at 1-3 mm constrain H2S, CH4 and ortho/para H2 abundances and the global circulation?

evidence.quote: agrees very well with both the ALMA millimeter and the 2003 VLA centimeter data from (cite: dePater2014).
At altitudes above 1 bar, we use the temperature profile from (cite: Fletcher2010).
We use the protosolar values from (cite: Asplund2009): C/H$_2$ = 5.90E-4; N/H$_2$ = 1.48E-4; O/H$_2$ = 1.07E-3; S/H$_2$ = 2.89E-5.
Between $32^{\circ}$S$-20^{\circ}$N, we use the (cite: Karkoschka2011) methane profile at $6^{\circ}$S; elsewhere, we use their $45^{\circ}$S model

recipe.method: Standard ALMA pipeline in CASA 5.1 followed by three rounds of self-calibration
key_parameters: Solution intervals: full observation, 350 s, 60 s

recipe.method: tclean MFS with natural weighting, circular mask, limb-darkened model subtraction
key_parameters: 512x512 pixels, 0.02" cell, 1000-2000 iterations until in-disk noise equals sky noise

recipe.goal: Measure disk-averaged brightness temperature and noise
recipe.method: Average of summed flux density within disk and Bessel-function fit to uv short-spacing amplitude; CMB correction; noise from RMS in four sky boxes

recipe.goal: Build nominal Radio-BEAR model and residual maps
recipe.method: 2D RT model maps on 9455 disk points interpolated to 0.02", convolved with elliptical Gaussian beam; maps scaled so disk average matches nominal model; subtract to get residuals; identify seven latitude bands
key_parameters: Dry adiabat, T=71.5 K at 1 bar, trace gases 30x protosolar (NH3 1x), intermediate H2
assumptions: Neptune's disk-average matches the nominal model; clouds ignored; LTE

recipe.goal: Fit H2S, CH4 and ortho/para H2 profiles per latitude bin
recipe.method: Grid of models varying one constituent at a time, then all together; best fit chosen via reduced chi2 per latitude bin
key_parameters: H2S deep 5-30xS in 5xS steps; supersaturation to 5-7 bar in 0.25 bar steps; CH4 0.55-4.4% in 0.36% steps
assumptions: Brightness variations due to opacity variations; no latitudinal temperature variations beyond dry adiabat

evidence.quote: We identify seven bands on Neptune that correspond to discrete changes in the temperature structure

answer_key.quantity: South polar cap best-fit deep H2S and CH4

evidence.quote: our best fit model depletes the deep atmospheric abundance of both H$_2$S to 1.5$\times$ the protosolar value and CH$_4$ to 0.55$\%$ (11.5$\times$S).

answer_key.quantity: Best-fit reduced chi2 per latitude bin (90S-66S to 20N-50N)

evidence.quote: are colder than the background by $\sim0.5-1.5$K in all three bands.
Our ALMA maps show average enhancements of $2-3$K in Bands 3 and 4

not_stated_but_needed: Limb-darkened model parameters used for subtraction
Self-calibration solution type and reference antenna
Exact method of fitting the Bessel function to uv short-spacing amplitudes
Method of selecting best-fit profile (grid search criteria beyond reduced chi2)
Planetary radius/ephemeris values used for sub-observer coordinates
missing_for_reproduction: Exact abundance profile definitions for supersat-v1/v2
score_reason: Public data and code with clear pipeline, but several modelling and imaging details are not stated.
rediscovery_reason: Data are from a known ALMA project, the recipe is mostly complete, code is public, and results (Tb, chi2, abundances) are numeric.
